title: Russia Approves $609B Three-Year Defense Budget as Germany Plans First Drone Regiment, Five European Nations Order 430 BAE CV90 Vehicles, and Taiwan Commissions Final Tuo Chiang Corvette
subhead: Moscow locks in 50.05 trillion rubles in military spending through 2029 while Berlin moves to establish a dedicated Bundeswehr drone regiment, Sweden leads a five-nation European order for more than 430 CV90 infantry fighting vehicles, and Taipei takes delivery of its twelfth Tuo Chiang-class missile corvette.

sections.heading: Russian State Duma Approves $609 Billion Three-Year Defense Budget as Germany Plans First Dedicated Drone Regiment
sections.body:
Russia's lower house of parliament, the State Duma, passed the country's 2027–2029 federal budget in its third and final reading, allocating 50.05 trillion rubles (approximately $609.3 billion) to national defense over the three-year period, according to Russian parliamentary records and defense industry assessments. The spending plan locks in wartime military production through the end of the decade even as Russian military prosecutors arrested a deputy commander of the Russian Aerospace Forces on corruption charges Thursday, Reuters reports.

In response to massed uncrewed warfare on the eastern flank, internal government documents show that Germany is preparing to establish the Bundeswehr's first dedicated drone regiment, integrating long-range strike munitions, tactical reconnaissance UAVs, interceptor drones, and electronic warfare units under a single command structure. Meanwhile, NATO authorized an additional AWACS radar aircraft deployment to Poland after prosecutors confirmed three Russian cruise missiles had impacted Polish territory during recent strikes, Euronews reports.
sections.whyItMatters: Commitments of $609 billion in Russian defense spending through 2029 confirm that Moscow is budgeting for sustained industrial warfare, accelerating Germany's institutional shift toward dedicated drone-regiment formations.

sections.heading: Five European Nations Join Forces for 430 BAE Systems CV90 Combat Vehicles as Royal Navy Orders $186 Million in Underwater Drones
sections.body:
A coalition of five European countries led by Sweden signed a joint procurement agreement to acquire more than 430 CV90 infantry fighting vehicles manufactured by BAE Systems Hägglunds, Anadolu Agency reports. The multinational order aggregates production lots to lower unit costs, standardize tracked armored logistics across Northern and Central Europe, and replenish inventories depleted by transfers to Ukraine.

In the maritime domain, the UK Ministry of Defence awarded US defense shipbuilder HII a $186 million contract to supply REMUS 620 autonomous underwater vehicles (AUVs) for the Royal Navy. The medium-class uncrewed submersibles will provide long-endurance mine countermeasures, undersea cable inspection, and seabed reconnaissance across the North Atlantic and European chokepoints.
sections.whyItMatters: Pooling European orders for 430+ CV90 armored vehicles overcomes fragmented national procurement cycles, while Britain's $186 million REMUS 620 buy reflects urgent NATO priority on protecting seabed pipelines and data cables.

sections.heading: Taiwan Navy Commissions Final Tuo Chiang-Class Missile Corvette as Raytheon Wins US Navy SLCM-N Nuclear Missile Contract
sections.body:
The Republic of China (Taiwan) Navy took delivery of ROCS Bao Jiang (PCG-632) from Lungteh Shipbuilding, completing its 12-ship order of Tuo Chiang-class stealth missile corvettes initiated a decade ago, USNI News reports. Designed as wave-piercing catamarans armed with subsonic Hsiung Feng II and supersonic Hsiung Feng III anti-ship missiles plus Sea Sword II air defense interceptors, the corvettes form the core of Taipei's asymmetric coastal strike doctrine.

In the United States, Raytheon won a new engineering and advanced development contract for the US Navy's Nuclear-Armed Sea-Launched Cruise Missile (SLCM-N) program, advancing subsystem integration and prototype demonstrations for a low-yield tactical nuclear deterrent deployed aboard attack submarines. Separately, USNI News reports that the White House Office of Management and Budget has requested special continuing-resolution funding anomalies for Ford-class aircraft carrier redesign work and new surface combatant studies.
sections.whyItMatters: Completing all 12 Tuo Chiang stealth catamarans gives Taiwan a dispersed, heavily armed anti-ship fleet tailored for strait denial, while Raytheon's SLCM-N contract accelerates the return of tactical nuclear cruise missiles to US Navy warships.

sections.heading: Turkish Intelligence Foils Cyber Espionage Ring Targeting Defense Firms as Ankara and Riyadh Sign Military R&D Pact
sections.body:
Turkey's National Intelligence Organization (MİT) dismantled a cyber espionage cell caught attempting to infiltrate the wireless networks of major Turkish defense industry primes and critical public institutions on behalf of a foreign intelligence service, resulting in the arrest of two suspects, Anadolu Agency and Daily Sabah report. The counterintelligence operation coincided with a new domestic procurement contract awarded by the Presidency of Defense Industries (SSB) to Otokar for 4x4 tactical wheeled armored vehicles scheduled for delivery through the end of 2028, while HAVELSAN achieved international AS 9100 Rev.D aerospace quality certification.

On the export and co-development front, SSB President Haluk Görgün and Saudi Arabia's General Authority for Defense Development (GADD) chief Faleh bin Abdullah Al-Sulaiman signed a defense R&D and technology cooperation memorandum in Ankara, Anadolu Agency reports. In Southeast Asia, Indonesia took delivery of its first KSR X33 uncrewed fast attack craft built by PT Lundin, with follow-on hulls slated to integrate ASELSAN mission systems and potentially ROKETSAN's ÇAKIR cruise missile, while Poland and Hungary held bilateral talks with Ankara to expand defense industrial partnerships.
sections.whyItMatters: As Turkish defense systems expand into Saudi joint R&D and Indonesian uncrewed naval strike boats, MİT's disruption of a wireless cyber-espionage cell near defense plants highlights intensifying foreign intelligence targeting of Turkey's R&D ecosystem.

sections.heading: Kuwait Drone Strike Kills Two Italian Rheinmetall Technicians as Ukraine Regrets Libyan Officer Deaths in Benghazi Attack
sections.body:
A kamikaze drone strike against a military facility in Kuwait killed two Italian technicians employed by the Italian subsidiary of German defense contractor Rheinmetall and injured four others working on an air defense system, SCMP, CBS News, and BBC report. While Western officials attributed the attack to Iranian-backed networks and the Saudi-led Arab Coalition intercepted another Houthi drone over southern Saudi Arabia following a strike alert at the Jazan oil refinery, Tehran denied any military involvement and proposed a joint investigation with Kuwait.

Meanwhile, Ukraine's Foreign Ministry issued an unusual statement expressing regret over the deaths of two Libyan naval officers serving under eastern commander Khalifa Haftar during Kyiv's November 22 naval drone strike that sank a Russian corvette in Benghazi port, Anadolu Agency and OilPrice report.
sections.whyItMatters: The killing of Rheinmetall field engineers in Kuwait exposes the physical vulnerability of Western defense contractors maintaining air defenses across the Gulf, while Kyiv's apology to Benghazi seeks to prevent its Mediterranean anti-Russian strikes from triggering diplomatic retaliation in North Africa.

sections.heading: Philippine Forces Deploy BrahMos Missiles in Luzon Strait Drills as Chinese Think Tank Flags US Subic Bay Revival
sections.body:
The Armed Forces of the Philippines deployed warships alongside an Indian-supplied BrahMos supersonic anti-ship cruise missile battery during live territorial defense drills focused on securing the Luzon Strait between the Philippines and Taiwan, USNI News reports. Simultaneously, the USS Makin Island Amphibious Ready Group, carrying the 13th Marine Expeditionary Unit, departed Singapore to patrol the Indian Ocean transit corridors.

The exercises drew sharp scrutiny from Beijing, where a Chinese defense think tank cited by the South China Morning Post warned that Washington is quietly converting Subic Bay back into an 'unbranded US military base' through commercial shipyard, logistics, and munitions storage leases capable of supporting operations in both the South China Sea and the Taiwan Strait. Separately, imagery emerged of Chinese defense prime Norinco testing a desert-camouflaged export modernization package for Soviet-era T-72 main battle tanks pitched as a low-cost alternative to the T-90.
sections.whyItMatters: Practicing Luzon Strait sea-denial with supersonic BrahMos batteries while expanding US dual-use logistics at Subic Bay tightens the maritime chokepoint linking the South China Sea to the southern approaches of Taiwan.

bottomLine: Russia's approval of a $609.3 billion defense budget for 2027–2029 and Germany's plan to stand up its first dedicated drone regiment underscore Europe's transition to long-term high-intensity force structures, further backed by a five-nation order for 430+ BAE CV90 combat vehicles. In the Indo-Pacific and Middle East, Taiwan's completion of its 12-ship Tuo Chiang missile corvette fleet, Philippine BrahMos drills in the Luzon Strait, and a fatal drone strike on Rheinmetall technicians in Kuwait highlight the global spread of precision missile and uncrewed maritime competition.
sources: Breaking Defense, Defense News, USNI News, The War Zone, Anadolu Agency, Reuters, SCMP, CBS News, BBC, Euronews, OilPrice, Daily Sabah, TRT World
